title: Free-floating Subdivisions
scope: Form and topical subdivisions of general application (Section F: topical, Section G: form); each entry's use_under states the categories of headings ("subjects" = all heading types) under which it may be used without editorial establishment
general_notes: Listed below are general free-floating form subdivisions and those topical subdivisions having general application, or an application not covered by the pattern and other lists of free-floating subdivisions outlined on p. 1. For subdivisions having applications governed solely by the other lists, consult the appropriate list(s). On this list, statements are given of the types of headings under which each subdivision may be used along with definitions of use in some cases. For subdivisions that may be used under all types of headings -- geographic, personal, corporate, title, and topical -- the statement reads, “Use under subjects.” Subdivisions authorized for use under topical headings may be used under appropriate headings tagged 150 as well as under headings with other tags that are divided by topical subdivisions. For subdivisions of general application that also appear on other special lists, all uses are enumerated here. See also references are provided between related subdivisions on this list. See also references to closely related subdivisions on other special lists are also given. Appearing with each subdivision are references to instruction sheets in the Subject Headings Manual which explain or mention its use.

LC practice (Section F): In 2025, the use of form subdivisions was phased out. Library of Congress catalogers assign Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT) to bring out the form(s) and/or genre(s) of the resource being cataloged. Therefore, the form subdivisions maintained on this list are not available for use by Library of Congress catalogers. Catalogers at institutions external to LC may use them as dictated by their own institutional policies.

LC practice (Section G): In early 2026, the use of form subdivisions was phased out. Library of Congress catalogers assign Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT) to bring out the form(s) and/or genre(s) of the resource being cataloged. Therefore, the form subdivisions maintained on this list are not available for use by Library of Congress catalogers. Catalogers at institutions external to LC may use them as dictated by their own institutional policies.
Most form subdivisions coded $v on the lists may also be used as topical subdivisions coded $x when assigned to works about the form (H 1095 sec. E.6).
Free-floating subdivisions that are authorized for further geographic subdivision have the notation (May Subd Geog) on the lists of free-floating subdivisions (H 1095 sec. E.5).

Converter note: entries 0-335 are Section F (Topical subdivisions of general application); the remaining entries are Section G (Form subdivisions). For multi-element rows whose subfield codes differ (e.g. "$x Abbreviations $v Dictionaries"), "subfield" gives the code of the last element; Section G entries are all typed "form".
